source: Australian Antarctic Program, Station Leaders for 2001, Australian Antarctic Magazine, Issue 1 (Autumn 2001)
method: The article identifies Robb Clifton as Macquarie Island's 2001 station leader and reports 15–20 people wintering across Australia's four isolated outposts. Apply the rounded midpoint of that published range (17.5, rounded to 18) to Macquarie Island; the per-station count is modeled, not enumerated. Assign all 18 to working age because no station-specific age breakdown is published.

source: CIA World Factbook 2001, Population field for Heard Island and McDonald Islands
method: The July 2001 estimate identifies the territory as uninhabited. Temporary scientific visits are excluded from the resident-population baseline; this is an explicit zero assumption, not a census count.

source: CIA World Factbook 2001, Population field for Ashmore and Cartier Islands
method: The July 2001 estimate reports no indigenous inhabitants and only seasonal caretakers. The scenario records zero permanent residents and excludes temporary caretakers; this is an explicit resident-population assumption, not a census count.

source: BITRE Regional Statistics Booklet 2003, Table 6
method: The official 2001 territory table reports four residents. It does not publish ages; all four are allocated to ages 15-64 as a small-island staffing assumption.

source: CIA World Factbook 2000, Paracel Islands
method: The 2000 edition estimates 2,000 people and describes scattered Chinese garrisons with no indigenous inhabitants. Carry this nearest numeric estimate into the 2001 scenario; assign all to ages 15-64 as an active garrison model. The 2001 edition retains the garrison note but gives no numeric headcount.

source: UNESCO Malpelo nomination; Colombian Navy presence
method: The map region center matches Malpelo. The UNESCO nomination reports no permanent inhabitants and six Colombian Navy soldiers at a time, rotated monthly; the Colombian Navy states the outpost has operated since 1986. Use six working-age stationed personnel as the 2001 scenario occupancy; this is a staffing model, not a resident census.

source: CIA World Factbook 2001, Western Sahara
method: Use the July 2001 estimate of 250,559 for the territory. The Factbook marks all three age bands unavailable; model them using the preserved legacy cohort proportions (about 39% ages 0-14, 58% ages 15-64, 3% ages 65+), not as census counts. The territory status is unresolved in the source.

source: INSEE, estimated population at 1 January 2001, French Guiana; INSEE/CES 1999 Census age table
method: Official INSEE total and broad ages give 74608 residents aged 0-19 and 9560 aged 60+. The 1999 age table at https://www.vie-publique.fr/files/rapport/pdf/014000573.pdf allocates 0-14 versus 15-19 within the under-20 band. Ages 65+ are estimated by splitting the 1999 60-74 group uniformly into 60-64 and 65-74, then retaining the 75+ group share within the 2001 60+ total; ages 15-64 are the residual. Cohort values are estimates, not a 2001 census cross-tabulation.

source: French National Assembly response on Eparses staffing (1 June 2010)
method: The 2010 parliamentary answer reports 45 military staff on Glorieuses, Juan de Nova, and Europa (15 per island), plus a five-person Météo-France team on Tromelin; Bassas da India is submerged at high tide. Model 50 working-age staff for the 2001 scenario based on the permanent detachments established in 1973. No family settlement is implied.

source: CIA World Factbook 2001; French Senate report on 1991 TAAF wintering
method: The Factbook says there were about 100 researchers across the Southern Lands in 1997, varying by season. Allocate that total across Kerguelen, Crozet, and Amsterdam using the 1991 Senate wintering distribution (88:41:35), yielding 54, 25, and 21. All are modeled working-age station personnel; Saint-Paul has no separate station.

source: INSEE, Mayotte population counts in the 1997 and 2002 censuses
method: Total is linearly interpolated between the official 1997 count of 131,320 and 2002 count of 160,265. No 2001 regional age profile was located; age cohorts retain the legacy shares and are explicitly modeled.

source: CIA World Factbook 2001; British Antarctic Survey station staffing
method: The 2001 Factbook records the military garrison withdrawal in March and replacement by a permanent BAS science group, plus a biological station on Bird Island. source: UK Parliament answers; Republic of Cyprus 2001 census; Council of Europe SBA base staffing
method: Combine 4,329 Cypriot civilians enumerated in Akrotiri in 2001 with an allocated share of the 7,800 UK military, UK-based civilian personnel, and dependents reported for the SBAs in 2004. Allocate the UK total using the published 2007 station military ratio (Akrotiri 1,300; Dhekelia 2,200). Model Cypriot civilian ages from the 2001 Republic of Cyprus age shares and UK base ages as 15% children, 83% working age, 2% older; not a local age census.

source: CIA World Factbook 2001, British Indian Ocean Territory
method: The 2001 Factbook reports no indigenous inhabitants and gives the latest numeric staffing observation as approximately 1,700 UK/US military personnel plus 1,500 civilian contractors on Diego Garcia in 1995. source: Government of Jammu and Kashmir, Regional Indicators 2016-17, Census 2001
method: Use the official 2001 Census total of 5,476,970 for the Kashmir Region. The cited table does not publish these three age bands at this geography; model them using the preserved regional cohort proportions and largest-remainder rounding, not as census counts.
